In the 3D-printed model without thermal compensation the AB was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0}.\mathbf{11}\pm \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{27}\mathbf{mm}$</tex>, the WB was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\mathbf{1}.\mathbf{89}\pm \mathbf{4}.\mathbf{68}\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}/\mathbf{mm}$</tex>, and the WAD was 7.85 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{4}.\mathbf{35}\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}/\mathbf{mm}$</tex>. The anthropomorphic 3D-printed models are an accurate instrument for the representation of the spatial properties of the skeleton. They can provide fast and reproducible results in morphometric studies on bone morphology. Thus 3D-printed models are a more reliable tool than the measurements of Volume renderings, which clinicians frequently use.*

articleTitle: Managing Cybersecurity Threats for Seniors' Digital Needs Using Age-Friendly Remote Healthcare Monitoring Model
abstract: Monitoring remotely the health and lifestyle of the seniors through smart devices brings some challenges due to the age-related impairments of the elderly or to the fact that the connected smart devices can be perceived as a vulnerable gateway to the whole digital system. Therefore, for mitigating the cybersecurity threats in such a healthcare model, the seniors' needs and specificities should be addressed (carefully, with priority and taking into consideration the sensitive feature of health and personal data) through continuously updated security mechanisms and protocols. This paper aims to present the most relevant aspects related to all these and to demonstrate how they have been implemented in a remote health monitoring system designed to support a healthy, active and independent life of a senior in a smart device-based home.

articleTitle: Reconstruction Techniques for Traumatic and Tumoral Bone Loss in Hand Surgery. Retrospective Study
abstract: The hand is frequently esposed to domestic or industrial traumas of varying complexity. The consequences of these traumas can be loss of soft tissues but also of bone. Bone loss also occurs after the tumors ablation. Bone reconstruction can be done with free transfer of vascularized bone, non-vascularized autologous bone or liquid or solid bone substitutes. We studied a group of patients in whom bone reconstruction after trauma or benign tumors (enchondroma) was done with autoulogous bone or bone substitutes.

articleTitle: Corrosion Reactivity in the Pre-clinical Study of 23 Grade Titanium Alloy in Ringer Solution
abstract: The properties of an implant or medical device are determined by the specific properties of the product, such as machinability, availability or appearance, as well as the properties of materials, such as good corrosion resistance to avoid degradation in the biological environment. Good biocompatibility assumes that no allergic or toxic reaction occurs through corrosive degradation. Titanium and its alloys are frequently used in medicine for the production of prostheses or pacemakers, orthopedic or dental implants, etc. The most popular titanium alloy that has been used since the 1980s is the Ti6Al4V alloy. The present research paper makes a pre - clinical study on the electrochemical reactivity of grade 23 titanium alloy (Ti6Al4V) in Ringer's solution. The alloy is used predominantly as biomedical devices or in the field of tissue engineering, such as bone plates or structural elements of femoral prostheses, due to their excellent corrosion resistance, good specific strength, high biocompatibility and non-magnetic properties compared to Ti Grade. The applied electrochemical methods are the evolution of the free potential for immersion in solution, linear polarization and potentiodynamic polarization as well as the measurement of the polarization resistance and the corrosion rate in time. Roughness and electronic microscopy micrographs are used to visualize the surface of the alloy before performing the tests.

articleTitle: Electrospinning Thinner Nanofibers Using Lasers
abstract: Thinner nanofibers can produce denser meshes and have numerous uses in biological and medical applications. We propose a novel improvement to the electrospinning process, a popular method to produce nanoscale fibers. Our setup consists of three laser diodes, which help focus the polymer jet, and results in almost 20 percent thinner fibers with increased fiber density. In our experiments, we show results for polyethylene oxide, which is a biocompatible and non-immunogenic polymer. However, our proposed method can easily be adapted to other synthetic and bio-polymers.

articleTitle: Optimization of Experimental Parameters for Co(II) Ions Biosorption onto Algae Biochars
abstract: In this study, the removal Co(II) ions from aqueous media using biochars obtained from the marine algae biomass is proposed. Due to the high content of carbon, marine algae biomass can be a suitable raw material for biochar production. Therefore, the biochars obtained by pyrolysis of algae biomass (Ulva lactuca sp.) at two different temperatures: 320°C (BC-320) and 550°C (BC-550) under limited oxygen conditions, were used as biosorbents for the removal of Co(II) ions in aqueous media. The biosorption process was examined as a function of initial pH, biosorbent dose, initial Co(II) ions concentration, contact time and temperature, and the optimal conditions were selected step by step. The highest biosorption efficiency for Co(II) ions was obtained at a pH of 5.0, biosorbent dose of 4.0 g/L, a contact time of 60 min and temperature of 22°C. Under these conditions, the experimental removal percent is higher than 99 %, when the initial concentration of Co(II) ions is in the range of 12- 71 mg/L.

articleTitle: Data on the Microbiota Found in a Murfatlar Vineyard in Two Different Disease Management Practices
abstract: This study was conducted in order to determine the influence of the disease management system on the microbiota found in a Murfatlar vineyard, where plots treated and untreated with phytosanitary products were established. The number of bacterial and fungal cells/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was determined using the method of epifluorescence microscopy, and soil fungi were isolated and identified using macroscopic and microscopic morphological criteria. Climatic data were monitored using IoT sensors installed in the studied plots, and soil macroelements semiquantitative analyses were performed in order to assess their influence of the obtained results. In all of the studied samples, the untreated plots harbored a greater density of microorganisms. The flowering phenophase showed the most significant number of microbial cells on the leaf surface, as well as the greatest number of UFC/g soil, results which are mainly due to the presence of precipitation and high humidity.

articleTitle: Recognition of Voice Commands using CNN for Romanian Language
abstract: In this paper, we studied the capability of the DLCNN (Deep Learning Convolutional Neural Network) classifier to be included into an intelligent human-machine interface. This interface will interact with a small number of people (generally one person, the owner of the device: autonomous car, smart home, intelligent wheelchairs, etc.). The main goal was to use a classifier capable of being trained quickly (maximum 10 training epochs), with a minimal set of training data. We need an algorithm of reasonable complexity, that can be integrated on small single-board computers (SBCs) like Raspberry Pi for example. We used 2 sets of voice commands, one in English and one in Romanian, which will train two different DL-CNNs. MFSC (mel-frequency spectral coefficients) coefficients did not provide the expected results, but with MFCC (mel-frequency cepstral coefficients) coefficients we obtained a 92% accuracy rate in the voice commands recognition.

articleTitle: Changes in Plantar Pressure Distribution Induced by RELIVE Overground Gait Rehabilitation System
abstract: Gait is mandatory for a good quality of life, being the reason why the interest in technology for gait rehabilitation is exponentially increasing. The RELIVE system is an overground gait training system in experimental model phase that controls weight offloading. The aim of this study is to evaluate the influence of the RELIVE system on plantar pressure distribution in order to contribute to its future development. We collected plantar pressure data using F-Scan from Tekscan and analyzed six regions of the foot (hallux, first metatarsal, second and third metatarsal, fourth and fifth metatarsal, medial calcaneus and lateral calcaneus) during 16 gait sessions, the majority within the RELIVE system and some out of the system, for comparison. The results suggest some strong points of the system, but also some aspects that need to be improved.

articleTitle: Volumetric Segmentation of Brain Tumors Using Neural Networks
abstract: Although medical images can provide exceptional anatomical views, distinguishing the pixels of lesions from those of healthy tissue remains one of the most challenging tasks in medical image analysis. This paper focuses on the task of automatic brain tumors segmentation from Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images. The aim of the study is to identify an optimal solution based on volumetric convolutional neural architectures, trained on the Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2020 dataset. This work presents some of the most popular Convolutional Neural Networks-like volumetric neural networks (Seg-Net 3D, U-Net 3D, ResUNet) used for automatic segmentation of brain tumors in a comparative manner and how they can be optimized to achieve maximum performance. The best Dice score results are obtained after training the ResUNet type network, which leads to a percentage of 91.4% for the whole tumor, while the U-Net network reaches a maximum value of Dice score of 90.8%. The worst results are obtained by using the SegNet architecture, that leads to a dice score of 90.4%.

articleTitle: Progressive Web App for Real-time Doctor-Patient Communication and Searchable Health Conditions
abstract: During the global pandemic, it became evident that remote healthcare is becoming increasingly important. Despite their functional features, designs, and accessibility, existing telehealth apps and websites can be costly to develop since they need to be written separately for each platform. A Progressive Web App provides the ability to develop an app which can be platform independent, which means it can be created with a single source code but run on a variety of devices. This paper reports development of a progressive web app which offers a secure platform to access up-to-date healthcare information, as well as offering real-time communication between patients and doctors. Details about the system architecture, features, and functionalities of the app, both online and offline, have been discussed from the perspective of the developers, as well as their advantages to end users.

articleTitle: 3D Bioprinted Methacrylated Gelatin-Based Scaffolds
abstract: Tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine, drug screening and diagnostic tools are just a few of the many biomedical applications that have employed 3D bioprinting since its widespread adoption. Biomaterials (gels and hydrogels) for 3D bioprinting should have shear-thinning properties, excellent printability, suitable mechanical capabilities, biocompatibility, and a straight forward crosslinking method. In this paper, bioprinted methacrylated gelatin-based hydrogels, crosslinked with poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate or di(ethylene glycol) diacrylate have been developed in order to be used as scaffolds in soft tissue engineering. Hydrogels are frequently scaffolded for use in tissue regeneration because of their 3D structure, high hydrophilicity, and macroporosity. The functional synthetic polymer/monomer interacted with methacrylated gelatin to significantly enhance pore diameter and hydrogel scaffolds susceptible to enzymatic attack under simulated physiological conditions of pH and temperature.

articleTitle: Smartphone PPG Validation for a Depression Assessment Protocol
abstract: A new smartphone application for pulse photoplethysmography (PPG) recording is validated for a depression assessment protocol, consisting of four stages that includes recordings of movement-related tasks, talking-related tasks, and stillness. The separation of these stages allows to evaluate the agreement between the PPG acquired using the smartphone camera and a commercial pulse oximeter, used as reference, in different conditions. Several time-domain and frequency-domain heart rate variability (HRV) metrics have been studied. Results suggest a strong agreement during stillness phases <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{r}\geq \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{96}\ (\mathbf{p} < \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{05})$</tex> for all the HRV metrics), as well as a moderate downgrade during movement and talking. The agreement is also different between low-frequency related metrics <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{r}\geq \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{92}\ (\mathbf{p} < \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{05})$</tex> and high-frequency related metrics <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{r} < \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{78}\ (\boldsymbol{p} < \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{05}))$</tex>. The overestimation of the high-frequency component of the HRV may be a limitation for smartphone PPG in depression monitoring.

articleTitle: Coronary Artery Segmentation on Echocardiograms for Kawasaki Disease Diagnosis
abstract: Symptoms such as vasculitis, myocarditis and coronary dilatation are possible consequences of Kawasaki disease. Damage to the blood vessels caused by these symptoms can lead to long-term heart problems. It is the most common acquired heart disease affecting young children in developed countries. One way to detect abnormalities in the coronary arteries caused by this disease is by monitoring patients with 2D echocardiograms. This monitoring must be performed manually due to the great difficulty of automation, as the spectrum of heart size and shape in infants can be very diverse. This paper presents a solution to help diagnose Kawasaki disease in a faster and simpler way by using convolutional neural networks. More specifically, this work can automatically segment coronary arteries from 2D echocardiography images. These frames are relevant as Kawasaki disease can be detected by measuring the opening of the coronary artery. Different U-net based models have been developed and evaluated. In addition, an echocardiogram dataset specific for Kawasaki disease has been created in collaboration with the Hospital 12 de Octubre in Madrid. This solution can be considered as another step in the development of a fully automated solution for diagnosis [1].

articleTitle: Slow Component Analysis Based Interictal-Preictal EEG Prediction
abstract: An accurate and compact epileptic seizure prediction system would be significant to intractable patients as it can significantly improve the quality of their lives. This paper presents a novel approach for prediction of seizures in epileptic patients based on scalp electroencephalography (EEG) recordings. In this study, we explored meaningful underlying representation to derive latent predictive characteristics of EEG signals, at the same time make it possible to design a lightweight, compact solution for seizure prediction. This paper proposes a novel approach that explores the underlying representation of the signals by introducing Slow Component Analysis (SCA) for the differentiation. In addition, extracting several epileptiform-band signals from the original EEGs prior to the slowness analysis helps find the intrinsic change of the brain states. The performance of the proposed methodology was evaluated with the publicly available CHB-MIT dataset. This method achieved an accuracy of 94.41%, a sensitivity of 94.27%, a specificity of 95.61%. The experimental evaluation indicated that the proposed lightweight solution has acceptably satisfactory prediction performance.

articleTitle: Data Analytics of Gait Monitoring from Parkinson's Disease Patients
abstract: Nowadays, Parkinson's disease starts to affect a lot of people, and is the second most common progressive neurological disorder. This paper aims to cover the monitoring and rehabilitation of Parkinson's Disease patients in remote areas. The data was recorded using a smartphone with an accelerometer function and processed to determine the absolute acceleration for each subject: the model, the control, and the target. The results obtained indicate that there is a difference between the healthy subjects, the model and control, and the target. This was determined by comparing the probability distribution function of the subjects and by making a geometrical implementation for the absolute acceleration).

articleTitle: Extraction of Active Compounds from Armoracia rusticana Using Maceration and Ultrasound Assisted Extraction
abstract: Current research in the food field is primarily focused on obtaining biologically active compounds to replace chemical food additive from food products. In this study, the active compounds from horseradish (Armoracia rusticana) were extracted by maceration and ultrasonic assisted extraction using two solvents, ethanol and methanol. For this extraction the compounds phenolic, antioxidant activity and vitamin C concentration were determined. The results showed that maceration is a slow method resulting in a low yield of the total polyphenols, unlike ultrasound assisted extraction. The results for antioxidant activity show that in the case of maceration, the solvent does not influence the extraction process and the maceration efficiency is between 35% and 50%. In the case of ultrasonic assisted extraction both the solvent and the ultrasound time influence the oxidative activity of the extracts. Extracts obtained by maceration and ultrasonication contain concentration between 10.7 and 24.4 mg vitamin C / 100 g. It can be stated that the ultrasound assisted extraction method could successfully replace the conventional extraction obtaining the highest content of polyphenolic compounds over a period of 30 minutes.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Applied to Counselling Programmes for Optimizing Self-Control in Teens. Case Study
abstract: The article describes a study run in 2021 on self-control in teens who study drama at ‘Dinu Lipatti’ Art College in Bucharest. The research introduces an online platform managed by artificial intelligence networks aimed to educate self-control for the target group that consisted of 90 students aged between 14 and 17 who study drama at the aforementioned institution. The purpose of the study was to identify if the techniques and exercises uploaded on the platform could produce any change in the teens' self-control after the period of three months of online practice. At the beginning of the program, the target group applied the Barratt questionnaire for impulsivity and the scores became referential for the analyses. After that, the adolescents made accounts on the platforms and worked the exercises for three months and at the end of the program they filled in the Barratt impulsivity questionnaire again. The initial scores were compared to the final scores using statistical methods. The results emphasized a good efficiency of the platform assisted by artificial intelligence. These findings encourage the following research to design platforms or applications dedicated to the needs that teenagers identify in order to help them improve the resilience during harsh periods or crises in their lives and to enhance self-development, as well.

articleTitle: A Multipurpose Video Immersion Laboratory
abstract: In the pandemic context of the last year and a half, there has been an increasing emphasis on the need to digitize teaching activities. This paper proposes a new concept of visual education based on visual immersion. A laboratory containing eleven video projectors commanded by a single computer is developed to create the immersion effect. While in this case, the advantages of the design are presented in bio-engineering class, it can be easily extended to any other discipline.

articleTitle: HAND AID: Hand Orthotic Device with Strength Monitoring System
abstract: Hand injuries are the most common type of workplace injury. Hand injuries are classified into several types, including cuts, fractures and dislocations, infections, and so on. If not treated properly or if medical attention is delayed, hand injuries can lead to serious injuries that can result in disability. The hand is a sensitive part of the human body. Even a minor injury to the hand may necessitate immediate medical attention, or it may lose function under certain conditions. HAND AID: Hand Orthotic Device with Strength Monitoring System, is a micro controller-based wearable - exoskeleton device for rehabilitation of hand injury. HAND AID is an assistive device that assists occupational therapists in carrying out therapy exercises. To monitor the patient's progress for each therapy session, the device uses servo motors to provide movement and a flex sensor to measure the patient's hand strength. The patient's measured hand strength will then be recorded in the database and graphed for a visual representation of the patient's progress. It can also be used as a form of exercise to keep one's mobility. As an expected output, the device must be able to assess the patient's hand strength in order to identify the patient's condition or situation and provide the necessary exercise. The system was tested for accuracy, dependability, and functionality. The device is expected to accurately identify the patient's hand strength and record it in the database. In terms of dependability, the device is expected to produce progress in terms of the patient's condition. Finally, for functionality, the device should perform all of the programmed exercises at the same time and without error. In terms of dependability, if the patient exercises his or her hand on a regular basis, progress will be visible. It is observed that the device serves its purpose in terms of functionality by providing exercises and recording the patient's progress.

articleTitle: Language Identification Models for Short Medical Texts
abstract: In the context of SARS-CoV-2 transmission prevention, the short texts on the social networks are full of abbreviations, technical medical terms, slang words that are outside the native languages or pejorative jargon. In other words, the language identification issues are not trivial. In fact, always this task remained a challenge for short texts originating from social media, which abounds in hard-to-understand sequences of letters. Moreover, when the whole world is facing a “medical crisis”, the situation must somehow be controlled in order for the panic to not degenerate even more. As a result, we need enhanced tools that can help us speed up the process of detection of linguistic aspects of the online content. This paper presents a new method intended to identify the language of a Twitter collection related to COVID-19 subject, based on AI algorithms. The aim of this work is to optimally determine the main language in which a text is written, with the constrains given by the diversity of the short text language found in tweets. Therefore, to find an optimal solution for language detection, we evaluated the impact of several language detection algorithms for short texts. Moreover, the results of this analysis were used for the implementation of a new language detection model, focused primarily on the detection of the Romanian language of the gathered tweets. The results suggest that a hybrid approach which combines classic techniques looks like a realistic direction of research.

articleTitle: Improved Classification of Benign and Malignant Breast Lesions Based on Contrast Manipulation and Gradient Map
abstract: This study proposes an approach to enhance the contrast breast ultrasound (BUS) images with the preservation of the finer details. The main idea is to use the relevant and most important features in the classification of BUS images as benign or malignant. Among the contrast manipulation techniques, both linear under- and overexposure methods, contrast limiting adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) method and homomorphic filtering are used. The gradient maps of original images are generated for further analysis. Also, the gradient maps of original images are improved by the local mean subtraction and divisive normalization. Eight structural features are extracted from each gradient map image type. The extracted features feed a Random Forest (RF) classifier to determine their relevance for BUS images classification. An accuracy of 97.12% has been obtained for improved gradient map images and 93.03% for gradient map images.

articleTitle: Threats and Opportunities Associated with the Implementation of Performance based Managed Entry Agreements in Slovakia
abstract: Slovakia has adopted an amendment to the of Act No. 363/2011 regulating, among other things, drug reimbursement and is undergoing a significant change in the availability of innovative treatments for patients. The main objective of this qualitative research was to analyse the opinions, views and perceptions of Slovak stakeholders with regard to performance-based managed entry agreements (PB-MEA) as facilitated by the recent amendment. The survey was carried out on a sample of 12 stakeholders. The responses were analysed using MAXQDATA 2022 software. The results showed that there are some positive expectations towards the nation-wide implementation of the PBMEA such as better availability of medicines, emphasis on the patient. A significant number of threats were also identified such as procedural unpreparedness and problems with data availability.

articleTitle: GAN Based Synthetic ECG for Psychological Stress
abstract: This paper presents a method for synthetic ECG generation using generative adversarial networks, GAN, for psychological stress. The aim is to study if generative adversarial networks can be used for psychological stress derived ECG generation. For testing the proposed method, we used a custom developed GAN adapted for 1D signals that was trained using both stress ECG and non-stress ECG. The results obtained indicate that generative adversarial networks can be used to generate synthetic stress-based ECG that has similar heart rate variability parameters as real stress ECG bio-signals.

Index Terms: Root Mean Square Of Successive Differences

articleTitle: Antibacterial Activity of Ocimum basilicum L. Extracts Grown in Aquaponic Conditions Against Gram-positive and Gram-negative Species
abstract: The practice of aquaponics is usually carried out in an integrated, recirculating system, which combines two components, aquaculture (fish farming) and hydroponics (plant culture). In this system, the nutrients required for plant growth result from the metabolism of the food by the fish. The experiment was carried out at the Dunărea de Jos University, Galati, where a significant biomass of basil (Ocimum basilicum) was obtained in an aquaponic regime, thus using the metabolic residues from intensive aquaculture. Basil (O. basilicum) is a fast-growing commercial crop commonly grown in aquaponic systems by commercial growers. The volatile oil of basil was isolated within the Discipline of Pharmacognosy, Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Medicine and Pharmacy Grigore T. Popa Iaşi, The evaluation of the antimicrobial activity of the volatile oil of basil (O. basilicum) cultivated in an aquaponic system on the bacteria Staphylococcus aureus (ATCC 25923) and Escherichia coli (ATCC 25922) was carried out at the Faculty of Biology, Alexandru Ioan Cuza University in Iaşi.

articleTitle: The Influence of Pleasant and Unpleasant Odours on the Acoustics of Speech
abstract: Olfaction, i. e., the sense of smell is referred to as the ‘emotional sense’, as it has been shown to elicit affective responses. Yet, its influence on speech production has not been investigated. In this paper, we introduce a novel speech-based smell recognition approach, drawing from the fields of speech emotion recognition and personalised machine learning. In particular, we collected a corpus of 40 female speakers reading 2 short stories while either no scent, unpleasant odour (fish), or pleasant odour (peach) is applied through a nose clip. Further, we present a machine learning pipeline for the extraction of data representations, model training, and personalisation of the trained models. In a leave-one-speaker-out cross-validation, our best models trained on state-of-the-art wav2vec features achieve a classification rate of 68 % when distinguishing between speech produced under the influence of negative scent and no applied scent. In addition, we highlight the importance of personalisation approaches, showing that a speaker-based feature normalisation substantially improves performance across the evaluated experiments. In summary, the presented results indicate that odours have a weak, but measurable effect on the acoustics of speech.

articleTitle: Burn Management using Enzymatic Debridement with Bromelain enriched Enzyme Mixture (Nexobrid™) - Case Series
abstract: Burns are complex injuries with multiple possible etiologies that can cause major morbidity and are associated with a high mortality risk. Bromelain-based Enzymatic Debridement has become a reliable and useful alternative to surgical debridement, which has been found to be most effective in mid- to deep dermal burns and mixed depth patterns. Enzymatic Debridement in circumferential burns to the extremity was studied by Fischer et al. who showed its effectiveness and safety for the prevention of compartment syndrome, reducing the need of surgical escharotomy. Our study included 10 patients aged 19 to 58 years of age, treated between October 2019 and September 2022. Enzymatic debridement is a viable alternative to surgical debridement that proves to have the advantages of rapid selective debridement and safety. Enzymatic debridement showed to be effective in circular lesions of the limbs, with no signs of compartment syndrome after the procedure, spontaneous reepithelization obtained, and no skin graft donor sites created.

articleTitle: A Smart Pillbox Integrated with an eHealth Platform
abstract: The current solutions imagined for medical compliance, either comprised of physical devices or software programs, still leave a lot of room for improvement. This work starts by presenting current developments and reviewing their capabilities. Next, we describe the implementation of a smart pillbox as part of a e-health platform capable of monitoring several physiological parameters. The pillbox has a modular design with detachable compartments which can be easily replaced and cleaned. A proprietary Android application is used for controlling the time and date of the pill administration while also generating reminders in order to ensure adherence to the prescribed medication. The integration with the e-heath platform is implemented at central server level which stores the events associated with the pillbox. Data integration with the monitored health parameters will provide evidence to the clinicians regarding the efficiency of the prescribed treatment.

articleTitle: Research on Measuring the Equivalent Electrical Parameters of the Epithelial Tissue using the Kinova Robot
abstract: We are attempting to investigate and measure the non-linear electrical properties of the skin-electrode interface at 1V voltages in order to better understand the physical processes that occur on the surface of the epithelial tissue at the skin-electrode contact. The purpose of this experimental model is to serve as a first step in the creation of a device. Two simple circuits were used, which are mounted on the same support that is attached to the Kinova robot. The electrodes are the same as those used in ECG investigations and are powered at a voltage of 1V at a frequency of 500 Hz. They are connected in series, in order to be able to determine the electrical parameters of the skin: series resistance (Rs), parallel resistance (Rp) and parallel capacity (Cp). The first circuit refers to a measurement on a normal epithelial tissue surface, and the equivalent electrical parameters to N are as follows: the series resistance will be RsN, the parallel resistance will be RpN, the parallel capacity CpN and the tissue resistance RbodyN. The tissue that requires investigation is labeled with IS from “Investigated Skin” and the equivalent parametersareas follows: the series resistance will be RsIS, the parallel resistance marked RpIS, the parallel capacity CpIS and the resistance of the tissue to be investigated will be RbodyI.

articleTitle: Nanopore Sensing for Proteins Involved in Disease
abstract: The development of fast, accurate and low-cost methods of analysis is increasingly necessary in the context of species evolution. Techniques based on the use of nanopores for the analysis of various disease-specific biomarkers have received attention from researchers. Studies have developed significantly, from the use of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> - HL protein pore to integrated devices such as the one developed by Oxford Nanopore Technology. The aim is to reach the full potential of using nanopores for clinical analysis, specifically to use them for various molecules regardless of their physicochemical properties (size, electric charge, concentration in solution). In this context, experimental protocols need to be adapted for each molecule to optimize biomarker analysis methods. Early and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective treatment leading to a higher quality of life. Changes at the structural level of proteins involved in various physiological processes cause dysfunctions and implicitly lead to the development of diseases such as Alzheimer's disease which is activated by the degradation of amyloid fibers. The challenge of analyzing proteins with nanopores consists precisely of their large structural size and non-uniform charge loading. The current paper aims to synthesize some of the knowledge in the field to aid in the challenges raised by the experimental part of nanopore sensing for proteins.

articleTitle: Developing a Versatile Framework Needed to Identify Pothole in Asphalt Using Deep Learning Algorithms
abstract: In recent years, interest and investment in cognitive systems and artificial intelligence has grown exponentially, and continues and will continue, both in academia, scientific research and technological development, and in the commercial and business world, from the most small to large corporations. The present paper aims to use a embedded computing boards from Nvidia, the Jetson Nano developer kit. It is a small, powerful computer designed to power entry-level edge AI applications and devices. The purpose of this approach is to develop a general framework for potholes identification. In this research a Jetson Nano board was used through which recording image is taken in real time by a video camera and to generate frames, in order to identify certain things that may occur in a city (i.e. asphalt potholes). The results of the study can provide to recognize the potholes that can cause traffic accidents or to transmit certain road malfunctions to a centralized information center.

articleTitle: Virtual Rehabilitation Program Using Kinect and Leap Motion Sensor Enhances Upper Limb Function in Stroke Patients
abstract: Virtual reality is being increasingly used in the field of rehabilitation. We tested the benefit of a non-immersive virtual rehabilitation program using the Kinect and Leap Motion sensor in the upper limb rehabilitation in subacute and chronic stroke patients. A total of 30 stroke survivors were randomly assigned in two groups in a 1:1 ratio. The active group benefited from 10 sessions of 30 minutes of virtual rehabilitation program added to the standard rehabilitation therapy. The control group received 10 sessions of 1.5 hours/day of standard rehabilitation therapy during their 14 days hospitalization. Upper limb function was assessed using the Action Research Arm Test (ARAT) and Upper Extremity Fugl-Meyer Assessment (UE-FM) at the beginning and at the end of the 14 days of study. The ARAT and UE-FM improvements were significantly higher in the active group compared to the control group. ARAT improvement was 8.13±5.74 points in the active group versus 2(0.25-2) points in the control group, p=0.0003. The UE-FM improvement was 6.86±3.11 points in the intervention group versus 2.2±1.14 points in the control group, p<0.0001. Virtual rehabilitation therapy was equally effective in the subacute and chronic stroke patients. In the subacute stroke patients, the ARAT improvement was 7.37±6.27 points versus 9±5.41 points in chronic stroke patients (p=0.6). UE-FM improvement in subacute stroke patients was 7.25±3.99 points versus 6.42±1.9 points in chronic patients (p=0.62). Conclusions: Non-immersive virtual reality program improved motor recovery in stroke patients. Both subacute and chronic patients benefited from the virtual therapy.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Apparatus for Body Thermal Reading and Hemoglobin Count Aggregated with a Mobile App
abstract: The non-invasive apparatus for acquiring the hemoglobin count and body thermal reading is developed as it is a pain-free prototype that mainly measures the hemoglobin count and body temperature of an individual. The prototype is integrated with a mobile application through wireless transmission so that the compilation of medical records is easily available and accessible to the doctor and medical experts. Proper authorization is assigned so that the confidentiality of data between the patient and the doctor is respected. The researchers came up with this concept because it is an innovative step in the medical field, adapting a paperless record keeping and monitoring of a patient's state that is useful for diagnosis. In this study, the researchers focused on thalassemia patients as they are somehow neglected in the Philippines. Tracking the hemoglobin count and body temperature is essential in the lives of thalassemia patients. Data accumulated can help the doctors perceive if he/ she is subjected for blood extraction, or even for diagnosis purposes. Thus, the study could provide a public awareness for the substantial importance of getting a regular health consultation, and lead to efficient management in clinics and hospitals across the Philippines.

articleTitle: Modelling the Mutually Exclusive Oncogenic Mechanism
abstract: We introduce reaction systems with mutual exclusion by adding to the known reaction systems a relation describing the mutual exclusion between rules. These new systems can describe mutual exclusivity in cancer genomes. We analyze the notion of reversibility (in both reaction systems and reaction systems with mutual exclusion), and prove some properties.

articleTitle: The Impact of Growth Media on Production and Volatile Oil Composition of Ocimum Basilicum L. Cultured in Aquaponic Conditions
abstract: The present research aims to reveal valuable information related to basil (Ocimum basilicum L.) volatile oil composition and production performance in aquaponics recirculating systems and to offer solutions for increasing the economic sustainability of this biotechnological process. Aquaponics substrate techniques is used considering 2 grow media - GM: conventional hydroton - HGM and alternative GM, using crushed seashells as by-products - AGM. The results indicate that AGM assures better basil growth performance in terms of weight, shoot height and leaves area surface. The yield of volatile oil from basil biomass indicates superior results for AGM (0.65 mL/100g basil dry weight - DW), compared to HGM (0.55 mL/100g basil DW). The volatile oil (VO) resulting from AGM basil recorded higher percentages of monoterpene (39.96%), aromatic compounds (9.93%) and aliphatic compounds (1.05%), compared to VO resulting from HGM basil (37.80% monoterpene, 8.5% aromatic compounds and 0% aliphatic compounds, respectively). It can be concluded that AGM represents a suitable solution for improving aquaponic basil production biotechnology both in terms of crop productivity and quality revealed by volatile oil composition.

articleTitle: 3D Printing for Improved Congenital Cardiovascular Pre-Procedural Assessment
abstract: 8 out of 1000 newborn suffer from a form of congenital cardiovascular disease. Complex congenital cardiovascular diseases require carefully pre-procedural preparation and heart-teams including imagers, surgeons, pediatric cardiologists, intensive-care and neonatal specialists. With the usage of 3D printing, the printing technician should be part of such a team. We report our experience regarding the steps taken in the treatment of an infant with complex congenital cardiovascular malformations requiring multiple surgeries and interventional procedures. The 3D data were extracted from a CT-based DICOM dataset, using commercially available software and printed using locally available material and hardware. Following multidisciplinary meetings, the patient underwent further treatment with good results.

articleTitle: RoCoFake - A Romanian Covid-19 Fake News Dataset
abstract: The Covid-19 pandemic, managed to shed light onto a neglected problem - that of fake news. Even though lockdowns were imposed in most parts of the world, collaboration between researchers across the globe wasn't impeded. Moreover, the lockdown has deprived people of face-to-face interactions and so they shifted towards online communication. This translated into a massive chatting data, which part was true, but fake information also had its share. Therefore, it is of great interest to develop a dataset to try to spot the fake information. RoCoFake comes to address the lack of resources in this domain, by providing a Romanian Covid-19 Fake News dataset, by aggregating various resources available online, like tweets, news titles and fact-checking news sites like factual.ro. This data provides researchers from the medical domain particularly, but not only, with a valuable, open-access data source useful for various research projects. A benchmark for fake news detection is also provided, so that future investigations can compare against our research. Results suggest that even though the dataset is relatively large, improvements can be made by incorporating retweets and comments.

articleTitle: Possible Understanding and Model-Based Prediction of Time Evolution of Number of Infected People in COVID-19 Pandemic in Japan
abstract: This paper analyzes the time evolution of the number of infected people in Japan since 2020, and important aspects are discovered. It is found out that the time evolution of the number of infected people exhibits two critical aspects of time evolution of infection; that is, the discovered specific intervals between the peak values and the valley values are useful in predicting the next peak. In addition, it is revealed that the time evolution of the increase in the number of infected people in Japan over the present 6th peak is non-linear, which is different from past characteristics since 2020. A possible background mechanism is discussed, and a possible prediction is also introduced.

articleTitle: Nuclear Division Index (NDI) in Peripheral Blood Lymphocytes Exposed to X-Rays and Its Interferences in the Biodosimetry of Medical Personnel Occupationally Exposed to Ionizing Radiation
abstract: The response to X-Rays by Nuclear Division Index (NDI) of peripheral blood lymphocytes was performed from a study group of general population. Two cell culture were initiated for each blood sample, being experimentally exposed at doses varying from 0,25 to 3 Gy. The NDI calculated revealed slight correlation to the gender-lower values for women. For occupationally exposed personnel to ionizing radiation, the average values of NDI, analyzed by gender or profession, were not correlated with micronucleus (MN/CBMN) test results. Beside gender, medication or health status related to lower NDI should be investigated, as literature provides.

articleTitle: A Sensitivity Analysis of Symbolic Dynamics indices for Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring
abstract: The assessment of fetal heart rate variability (FHRV) is fundamental for evaluating fetal well-being during pregnancy. Through cardiotocography (CTG), it is possible to monitor both the fetal heart rate (FHR) and the uterine contractions (UC) and, through the use og computerized analysis, it is also possible to extract synthetic parameters of the FHRV. Among the available FHRV indices, the use of symbolic dynamics (SD) arises as a promising nonlinear indicator to investigate the complexity in FHRV signals. However, there is not enough evidence of the reliability of such indices and no consensus on the proposed formula to compute them. Based on previous works on this topic, here we aim at carrying out a sensitivity analysis of one of the proposed SD parameters for FHRV analysis, namely the Variability Index (VI). A database of 583 CTG signals has been used as basis for this study. The signals were preprocessed and analyzed to extract the FHRV series and calculate the VI according to a predefined set of weights. Then, the weights have been systematically varied and the sensitivity of the obtained VI in discriminating different fetal conditions and signal characteristics was assessed by means of a statistical approach. The results obtained show that the choice of weights can be decisive for specific purposes, e.g. in evaluating fetal development and distinguishing cesarean from spontaneous sections. On the other hand, weights do not alter the VI sensitivity in discriminating between active and rest states, presence and absence of accelerations.

articleTitle: Glaucoma Detection using Fundus Images with Mimetic Anisotropic Filtering and Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Vision is an extremely important sense and its care is vital for the prevention of diseases that can end in irreversible blindness. The disease discussed in this paper is glaucoma, which has a worldwide incidence and it is ranked in the first places in causes of blindness. To contribute to the screening of people who can be suffering from this disease, this work aims to support ophthalmologists by means of an automated algorithm that combines preprocessing of images of the fundus of the eye with mimetic anisotropic filtering, and regression through convolutional neural networks. In this work we demonstrate that by doing the preprocessing with the mimetic anisotropic filtering before passing the images to the convolutional neural networks, we obtain an increase of 1.5% in precision and an increase of 3.27% in sensitivity.

articleTitle: A Content Analysis of Teachers Reaction Towards the Aggressors: Some Preliminary Results
abstract: A recent report from the Peruvian government indicated that 39 315 cases of bullying incidents have been reported between 2013 and 2020. Despite that this phenomenon is considered a public health issue, it is still a major problem in Peruvian public schools. Additional factors such as poverty and lack of training in bullying management among teachers seems to be contributing factors. Previous studies have found that teachers use a variety of strategies in relation to bullying incidents and that these have positive or negative impact in aggressors' behavior. Therefore, the present research aimed to describe and analyze how elementary Peruvian teachers react towards the aggressor in bullying incidents. To reach this goal, teachers completed open-ended questions of hypothetical physical bullying situations as well as sociodemographic items. Results showed that teachers used different strategies to handle physical bullying and that they had limited knowledge in how to approach these situations. These preliminary results are discussed in terms of research, possible practical applications for teachers and schools.

articleTitle: Patient Satisfaction with Online Pharmacy Services
abstract: This study described the satisfaction levels of 323 patients regarding the online pharmacy services. The level of patient satisfaction was high regarding the online pharmacy services in general (67.8% of respondents), the price of medicines (70.9% of respondents), the transport charges (55.1% of respondents), home delivery of medicines (62.5% among respondents), as well as the professional skills of pharmacists (77.7%, among respondents). A low level of patient satisfaction was recorded regarding the advice received by phone (47.1% of respondents) or e-mail (48.3% of respondents) from pharmacists with information about their drugs. We found statistically significant differences between some patient responses caused by socio-demographic variables, patient characteristics and frequency of accessing this service (p<0.05). The study revealed a positive impact on Romanian patients regarding the use of online pharmacy services, but the quality of patient counselling should be improved by applying effective and specific policies.

articleTitle: Isotherm and Kinetic Modeling of Hg(II) Ions Adsorption on PET-clay Adsorbent Materials
abstract: Inorganic and organic wastes have received increasing interests in decontamination process of industrial effluents containing heavy metals, because are cost-effective and eco-friendly. In this study, a new adsorbent, obtained by mixing clay with PET flakes (ration 1:5) was tested for removal of Hg(II) ions from aqueous solutions, compared with PET and clay. The influence of contact time and initial concentration on Hg(II) removal efficiency was evaluated by batch technique. Pseudo-second order kinetic model best described the experimental data (0.9985 < R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><0.9998). Langmuir and Freundlich models were used to describe the experimental isotherms. The experimental results show that PET-clay adsorbent has a much higher maximum adsorption capacity (312.50 mg/g) for Hg(II) ions, compared with clay (51.28 mg/g) and PET (8.89 mg/g) materials.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Use of Imaging Methods in the Diagnosis of Implant Rupture
abstract: The study aimed to investigate the use of imaging methods that can assess the integrity of the implant and confirm possible rupture, unlike clinical examination. The sensitivity and specificity of ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging were analyzed based on available studies. Magnetic resonance image has been found to have higher specificity and sensitivity compared to ultrasound.

articleTitle: Modeling and Experimental Didactic Solution for Analysing the Arterial Stenosis
abstract: This paper presents a didactic solution for arterial stenosis analysis that contains mathematical modelling, practical implementation and functional simulation which can provide an easy learning solution for medical, biomedical engineering, or other related branches of students and researchers. For this purpose, several steps are followed, starting with an image captured from an angiography. With the aid of a dedicated software, a mesh will be created, and after a CAD defeaturing process, the blood vessel model will be imported in a simulation program, where real conditions will be analyzed. The next step consists in implementing a flow phantom that will be used for functional simulations. The experimental artery segment will be included in the experimental setup, allowing closer analysis of the pressure by controlling the fluid flow parameters in the probe. With the help of a data acquisition board, signals from the sensors are acquired, processed and displayed using the virtual instrument. Results obtained from mathematical modelling are presented along with user interface captures from two distinct experimental simulations with imposed parameters through the electronic control unit: adjustable fluid flow and pulse sensor synchronized fluid flow.

articleTitle: Partially Autonomous Information System Facilitating Performance-based Managed Entry Agreements in Slovakia
abstract: Performance-Based Managed Entry Agreements (PB MEAs) are agreements between payers and/or regulators on one and health technology businesses on the other end in which the individual patient's treatment success rate is monitored. Agreed reimbursement is determined by that rate. Without a successful response to treatment, reimbursement is reduced or completely absent. There is a high need for functional PB MEA systems across the developed economies. Satisfactory wide use has not yet been achieved. The reason is, among other things, technical obstacles and lack of adaptability of existing IT and data systems to the purpose of PB MEA. We present an autonomous cloud-based e-health information system to facilitate a transfer, data aggregation and analysis of real-world drug effectiveness data for the sake of PB MEA execution. The system makes use of a Pretty Good Privacy security feature for encrypting and decrypting and existing national e-health authentication cards.

articleTitle: KIR Analysis in Context of Kidney Transplantation
abstract: NK cells express activating and inhibitory killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptors (KIR). We analyzed the KIR genotypes in patients with kidney transplant and in healthy donor. We studied KIR in 84 Kidney transplant patients and 97 voluntary blood donors of stem cells. We evaluated 16 KIR genes, using the PCR-SSP assay. We found a risk association for activating gene KIR2DS5 and gene KIR3DS1 for acute kidney allograft rejection (AKAR) cases. Gene KIR3DL1 and gene KIR2DS4 conferred protection against rejection. This study suggests that we could exploit NK cell alloreactivity as a part of the optimization of recipient selection for kidney transplantation. Reducing the frequency of activation NK cell receptor genes can lead to a weakening kidney allograft rejection.

articleTitle: Epileptic Electrocorticogram Signal Detections with Patient-Specific Quantized Convolution Neural Network Models on the Edge TPU device
abstract: The closed-loop systems with neural stimulation and monitoring can be a promising tool of treatment for intractable epilepsies. Machine learning approaches to build patient-specific seizure detection algorisms has been collecting much attention, but implementation of the algorithms in the resource-constrained closed-loop systems has been challenging. In the present, we employed the Edge TPU device recently introduced by Google LLC to implement and test the patient-specific deep convolutional neural network models for the epileptic electrocorticogram signal detections. The present results suggested that the edge computing devices like the one we used here are useful for the real-time seizure detection, at least in some cases of the epilepsy patients.

articleTitle: Melanoma Detection using a Random Forest Algorithm
abstract: In recent years, statistical evidence has identified melanoma as a major cause of skin cancer deaths. In this study, we propose a skin analysis lesions based on colour features (C) and Hu (H) moments to differentiate benign (nevi) and malignant (melanoma) lesions and, a classification based on Random Forest algorithm. Colour features are found as follows. Pre-processing for hair removing using the Dull-razor method; image segmentation based on the optimal colour threshold set on each RGB colour channel (red, green, blue); 23 colour features extraction using the minimum and maximum RGB intensity and Hu moments; Random Forest (RF) algorithm to accurately differentiate benign and malignant skin lesions. This study used three datasets: 7-Point, Med-Node, PH2. RF classifier performance in terms of accuracy was: 94% for the 7-point dataset with H5, H7, H6, H2, C08 selected as relevant features; 98.1% for the Med-Node dataset and H7, H5, H6, H2, H1 ACC the relevant features; and, 96.5% for the PH2 dataset and H5, H6, H7, C03, H1 selected as relevant features, respectively. Shape features based on Hu moments are found to improve the classification performance of the skin lesions compared to the colour features.

articleTitle: Coping with Missing Values in Medical Data Sets: A Proposal of an Approach Based on Soft Clustering and Measures of Central Tendency
abstract: Medical data presents several hidden challenges compared to conventional datasets, the first challenge we encounter before even considering data processing and analysis is the presence of missing values in datasets. In this paper, we present a theoretical framework for missing values imputation through a fuzzy c-means machine learning clustering algorithm and statistical measures of central tendency, namely mean, median and mode. The algorithm of the proposed approach along with the experimental design is presented, aiming to evaluate the performance of the proposed missing values imputation on different medical datasets from the University of California Irvine Machine Learning Repository.

articleTitle: Method of Determining The Anxiety Level through EEG Wave Processing
abstract: In this article, we determine the level of anxiety by the questionnaire method (using the CAS test battery) and by the psychophysiological method of processing brain waves. The study's hypotheses examine the correlations between the psychophysiological method's anxiety level and the CAS anxiety level.

articleTitle: Sponge City As A Civil Engineering Solution To Climate Change That Improves Urban Flood Resilience
abstract: Climate change and urbanization drive the demand for water management to make cities more water resilient. Climate change brings heavy precipitation and causes urban flooding, with conventional construction of cities no longer suitable given the rising risk of flooding. Characterized by constructing cities as large sponges that absorb and treat water, the idea of sponge cities is a solution to stormwater control and drainage water management, which can be achieved by creating water absorbing areas, increasing permeable surface, and integrating stormwater and drainage systems. To assess flood resilience, evaluation indicators have been introduced to measure the effectiveness of sponge cities. A case study was also provided in this review to demonstrate how the concept of sponge cities was put into practice.

articleTitle: Systematic Review of the Sexual Education Impact and Reproductive Health on Adolescents
abstract: In order to determine the impact of sexual and reproductive health education on adolescents, a systematic analysis of 40 articles published and found in databases such as Scopus, Dialnet, Redalyc, Scielo, Google Scholar and Science was carried out. Direct; of the last 8 years. In them, different perceptions, needs, expectations, risk behaviors and level of knowledge of adolescents were identified; Likewise, intervention strategies were distinguished for the different cases. Through the selected articles, it is possible to learn more about the problem and reality of sexual reproductive education aimed at adolescents; and thus establish what changes should be implemented. Keywords: Adolescents, sexual health, educational talks, sexual education, public health, social problem, educational intervention.

articleTitle: Parallel vs Distributed Edge Detection for Large Medical Image Datasets
abstract: The medical routine of the future is strongly influenced by medical information technology. The quality and efficiency of medicine are at higher standards due to the image-based methods and the increase in computation power. Parallel and distributed computing are attractive alternatives to improve processing performance in many areas of study and this paper investigates such solutions for increasing the throughput on large datasets in medical imaging. In this research, different edge detection techniques are used for image processing, as it is the most common and challenging task in the medical domain. The results are relevant and present the effectiveness of the two processing approaches compared to a single CPU for the acceleration of medical image processing. The CUDA processing platform using a hybrid streams-based programming model is the parallel approach. The distributed system is a Linux-based cluster, which uses message passing for communication and efficient load balancing between nodes for high performance. This paper highlights parallel computing as a very good solution for processing large image datasets in the medical domain. Good results were also obtained for the distributed system.

articleTitle: Intelligent System for Automatic Assessment and Interpretation of Disguised Behaviour for Critical Infrastructure Personnel
abstract: This work involves the development of an innovative product aimed at critical infrastructure operators that will bring contributions to the respective sectors in terms of the level of research, technological development, and innovation (RDI). Critical infrastructures are essential at both enterprise and national levels. Any issue related to their operability can significantly impact many areas that depend on them. Developing an intelligent system for automatic assessment and interpretation of disguised behavior for critical infrastructure personnel will create the framework for rapidly defining each specific situation and taking the necessary prophylactic measures. The technical solution implements a neural network architecture for classifying human gestures and emotions using data collected from various sensors. The project also establishes a unique combination of the latest biometric and biosignal processing techniques with an NN approach for the near real-time analysis of emotions and behavior.

articleTitle: Influence of the Deposition Method on the Tribological Parameters of the Biocompatible Thin Films
abstract: Deposition of micro and nanostructured thin films is a solution for reducing the wear and increase the operational time for the biomedical implants' components. Tribological tests were performed to determine the friction coefficient and the wear rate of micro and nanostructured thin films deposited on M30NW steel and CoCr substrates by physical techniques. TiO2, TiN and CrN thin films with various thicknesses were deposited by DC sputtering, High Power Impulse Magnetron Sputtering and cathodic arc techniques. The quality of the deposited material and the dependence on the deposition technique was assessed by tribological characterization and the comparative analysis of the experimental results. TiN thin films deposited by cathodic arc, and TiO2 and CrN thin films deposited by DC sputtering, on both types of substrates, showed superior tribological parameters. After analyzing the data, it was concluded that DC sputtering is the most suited deposition method for this application.

articleTitle: An Educational Device Dedicated to People with Hearing Impairment
abstract: This paper presents an educational device used to help the learning of the people with ear impairment. The device uses two different sensors (gyroscope/accelerometer and tactile) connected to the microcontroller. The measured values from the sensors are transmitted to a PC that uses Node.js to process the information and the results are published in a web application. In this way other people can interact with people with hearing loss and the educational process can be improved.

articleTitle: Alginate Dental Impression Materials with Allantoin Enrichment: A Morphology, Dynamic Vapor Sorption And Swelling Evaluation
abstract: This study's objective is to evaluate several alginate impression materials used in dental medicine before and after Allantoin enriching in order to study their properties regarding the morphology, the swelling behavior in glutaraldehyde and simulated salivary fluid, as well as the dynamic vapor sorption capacity.

articleTitle: Smart Scan of Blood Test Documents to be Integrated in a mHealth Application
abstract: Controlling the physiological evolution of people plays an important role in the prevention and detection of health problems. Often, the medical analyzes performed by people are stored in documents that in the long term tend to be lost, suffer wear and tear and most importantly, do not facilitate the comparison of data to assess the physiological evolution. This work proposes an intelligent scanning system for blood test documents. This type of component can be found in digital (Digitally created PDFs, scanned PDFs and images) or physical format. It is intended to extract from this type of documents only the essential information, consisting of the blood components and their concentration. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) Machine Learning (ML) Kit was used to extract relevant information from documents in the case of scanned PDF's (SPDFs), images, and physical documents, and Apache's PdfBox for digitally created PDF's (DCPDFs). To filter the data and associate the blood constituents detected with the respective concentrations, a condition tree was developed. In the end, the methods used were able to detect an average of 95.38% of the blood compounds present in the different document formats. On average, 87.63% of the concentrations were correctly associated with the detected compounds.

articleTitle: Production and Properties of Needleless Electrospun Polycaprolactone and Self-Assembly Peptide Nanofiber Scaffold
abstract: Traditional therapeutics of organ and tissue deficiencies are organ transplantation, surgical reconstruction, synthetic prostheses, medical devices, etc. which are constrained by donor availability or inadequate performance of impaired organs or tissues. Tissue Engineering TE has been wherefore utilized as the alternate of conventional treatments of pathological obstacles considering its superiorities like harmonious with regional organs or tissues, optimal degeneration time with the rebirth of novel structures, prompting cell adhesiveness, procreation and differential of cells in tissue scaffolds and others. Artificial polymers like polycaprolactone (PCL) with nature materials like peptides have been introduced to fabricate nanofiber scaffolds. In this work, porous PCL scaffolds were foremost engineered to examine fiber morphology. SEM images showed that different fiber roughness and fiber spin were observed from different fibers within the same sample. Latterly, PCL/P11-4 polymer solutions were prepared to fabricate nanofiber scaffolds. P11-4 was unevenly distributed in PCL scaffolds. PCL nanofiber substances enriched with peptides were emerged to each other. Some of the P11-4 fibers were broken in PCL nanofiber scaffolds.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Networks Screening for JWH Synthetic Cannabinoids: a Comparative Analysis Regarding their Specificity and Accuracy
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of the dataset size and of the number of molecular descriptors selected to build Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) screening for JWH synthetic cannabinoids. The aim is to determine how to most economically use the available data on these illicit drugs and still avoid overfitting. The results indicate a proportional decrease in the number of inputs in terms of memory requirements, processing speed, and numerical precision by fitting a model with the same database of designer drugs and the same test set for each different sized training dataset (having 100, 50 and 25 samples respectively). The results indicate that the model trained with 100 samples performs nearly as well as the reference ANN system (built with 150 samples), but only modest results are recorded for training sets consisting of 50 or 25 samples.

articleTitle: Dynamic Selection Classification for Chest X-Ray Images
abstract: In this article, we investigate how well combinations of classifiers work on chest X-ray images when using classical extracted features and deep learning generated features. We employed four methods for classical feature extraction and seven types of features generated with some well-known pre-trained neural networks. A dynamic selection of classifiers method based on accuracy is used for mixing these eleven classification results. The classification results are computed with a linear SVM (Support Vector Machine) using these eleven sets of features. For experiments, we employed the Kermany dataset that contains chest X-ray images of the lungs. In all situations, the combination of classifiers improved the individual results (up to 7% in the best case).

articleTitle: Nonlinear Hyperbolic PDE-based Filter for Mixed Poisson-Gaussian Noise Removal from X-ray Images
abstract: A nonlinear partial differential equation (PDE) – based mixed noise reduction technique for medical X-Ray images is proposed in this paper. The filtering approach uses a novel well-posed second-order hyperbolic PDE model that is solved numerically applying a fast-converging finite difference method-based discretization algorithm. This iterative numerical approximation scheme restores successfully the medical images affected by mixtures of noise, since it removes properly both the Gaussian and Poisson noise. The effectiveness of the introduced technique is illustrated by the restoration experiments and method comparison described in this work.

articleTitle: Discrete Event Simulation to Improve Clinical Consultations in a Rehabilitation Cardiology Unit
abstract: In recent years there has been a progressive growth in cardiological comorbidities. In this context, cardiological consultations assume a relevant importance in healthcare settings for assessing the patient before performing clinical procedures or administering treatments. The quality in cardiological consultation lies also in timely and accurate medical visits as early diagnosis enables prompt interventions that can improve the overall patients' stay in the hospital. The reduction of the time to deliver a cardiological consultation in hospital settings is therefore an indicator of the overall quality of the consultation service. In this work, discrete event simulation was used to analyze and improve the medical consultation process in a Complex Operative Unit of Rehabilitation Cardiology. The proposed approach allowed the identification of critical issues in the consultation process and assess possible improvement actions to be implemented in order to reduce the waiting time for cardiological consultations in rehabilitation cardiology. By the adoption of discrete event simulation models, a continuous monitoring of the quality of assistance can be achieved, thus enabling improvements in the quality of care from both clinical and organizational perspective.

articleTitle: Cephalometric Third Maxillary Molar Assessment Before and After Orthodontic Treatment
abstract: The aim of this study was to assess the changes in inclination and in the available posterior space for the third maxillary molar before and after orthodontic treatment. The study sample consisted of 104 adolescent orthodontic patients, mean age 13.96 years who finished their treatment in an average period of time of 26 months; 64 patients had no extractions and 40 patients had extractions of upper first premolars for orthodontic reasons. On the lateral cephalogram we established the Angle class of malocclusion for each patient and we measured the distance between the distal face of the upper first molar and the vertical pterygoid plane to evaluate the posterior space. The third molar inclination was evaluated by the angle between the tangent to the occlusal face of the tooth and the plane between the anterior and maxillary plane. Our results showed that the posterior available space registered a statistically significant increase during orthodontic treatment (p<0.5), especially for patients with favourable condition at the beginning of the therapy. There is no correlation between the changes in the distal space and class of malocclusion, although greater increase was found for II class malocclusion patients. Regarding third molar inclination before and after orthodontic treatment, the differences were not relevant, even in the extraction group, which means that first upper premolar removal does not change significantly statistic third maxillary prognosis for eruption.

articleTitle: Control Dynamics of the Generated Frohlich Photons by Biological System
abstract: In this paper we discuss a possibility of control of the dynamics of a biological medium that is radiated with an external millimeter wave source. We demonstrate that for some internal and external parameters the evolution of the system displays continue periodic and chaotic behaviors.

articleTitle: Method for Diagnosing The Level of Depression Compared with The Classical Method
abstract: In the article we determine the level of depression by the questionnaire method (using the CAS test battery) and by the psychophysiological method of processing EEG waves. We analyzed the correlations between the EEG waves (delta, theta, alpha and beta) as well as the relationships between the EEG waves from AF3 and AF4 sensors. Results previously obtained by other researchers are confirmed and we bring news regarding the direction and intensity of the relationship between EEG wave types and depression level. Advances in technology have made the EEG a widely used tool for non-invasive studies of neurological disorders, including depression. In this study we used Electroencephalogram (EEG) to determine measurable or quantifiable characteristics, used for diagnosis or determining treatment progress. The article formulates the conclusions obtained by analyzing the results of 24 subjects who answered the DAS depression questionnaire and were scanned with Emotiv EPOC X with 14 Sensors.

articleTitle: Corticosteroids in the Early Treatment of Covid-19: Feasibility Study of the Use of Czech Administrative Data in an Real-World Outcomes Evaluation
abstract: In this study, we used administrative data of six health insurance companies in the Czech Republic, to analyse the incidence of hospitalization in COVID-19 patients early treated with corticosteroids (CS). Cohort selection was based on index date defined by the date of the PCR test reported with COVID-19-related ICD-10 diagnoses found within a period of March 2020 - November 2020. The CS treated cohort was defined patients treated with CS within the 7 days after index date with no history of antibiotics nor corticosteroids within 30 days before index date. The control groups were defined either with or without a use of codeine within the 7 days after index date but always with no use of antibiotics nor corticosteroids within 30 days before and within the 7 days after index date. In total 590 274 records fulfilled the inclusion criteria, of whom 3 670 (0.62%) were hospitalized and 2 467 (0.42<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) used CS within 7 days after ID. The contrast between a studied medication and a control was analysed with the logistic regression analysis with adjustment on age. Treatment with CS as compared with a cohort of patients with no curative treatment was associated with significantly (Chi square test p<.0001) increased rate of hospitalization in those treated with CS with odds ratio calculated as 3.1. Compared with a cohort of patients taking codeine the CS was associated with significantly (Chi square test p=0.001) lower rate of hospitalization, giving a moderate odds ratio 0.6. No beneficial effect of CS can be concluded based on this study. The strong influence of the composition of the control group is also evident from this study, as is evident from the reverse effect of the use of codeine in the control group.

articleTitle: Electrophysiological Biomarkers of Epileptic Tissue in Human Brain Epilepsy
abstract: Objective: Localization and mapping of seizure-generating brain tissue, i.e., seizure onset zone (SOZ) is essential to ensure an excellent patient outcome after surgical resection. The clinical approach is to record spontaneous seizures with intracranial EEG (iEEG) and determine SOZ. However, this practice is burdened by inter-patient variability, temporal variability, time-consuming data annotation, and long and variable waiting period for seizures to happen. Approach: Here, we use data from intracranial monitoring of 28 patients with neocortical focal epilepsy. Kurtosis, complexity, activity, mobility, mean, median, min, max, peak to peak, variance, standard deviation, root mean square, and interquartile were extracted as features from the time domain in two frequency bands (12–55 Hz and 55–80 Hz). The features were extracted from segments of inter-ictal iEEG from 8962 channels and tested by Wilcoxon rank sum test with Bonferroni correction of alpha to compare if mean of the feature differs in SOZ versus non-SOZ in each patient individually. Results: From all features, kurtosis, maximum, minimum, peak to peak, standard deviation, root mean square, variance, interquartile shown consistent differences between SOZ and non-SOZ channels across patients (p<0.0004). Conclusion: We analyzed several iEEG time domain features and we found features that significantly differ for data recorded from SOZ channels in most of the dataset with the same trend across patients. Such features can help to automatically differentiate between SOZ and non-SOZ electrodes and a combination of multiple features can yield better classification performance to discover epileptic foci using inter-ictal data without waiting for seizure to be recorded.

articleTitle: The Localization of the Epileptogenic Zone from the Interictal Electroencephalogram
abstract: In the case of patients diagnosed with focal epilepsy, to establish a diagnosis and a treatment, it is necessary to know the source area in the patient's brain where the epileptic seizure is generated. In current clinical practice, these areas are detected by invasive methods such as electrocorticogram, combined with magnetic resonance imaging methods, which subject the patient to discomfort during the procedure. The supporting paper proposes the localization of epileptic foci in a more friendly way based on electroencephalographic (EEG) signals acquired non-invasively. The article approaches various models of inverse problems, aiming to achieve a spatial identification of the epileptogenic areas as precisely as possible, then projected on a three-dimensional model of the cortex and tomographic images. The results are compared with those obtained by doctors through invasive methods found in the support database. This analysis aims to classify the methods related to the diagnosis established by the medical personnel.

articleTitle: Attention Predictions Related to Cinematic Montage Using Biometric Markers with Application in ADHD Disorder
