abstract: The following case study targets the live deconstruction of a visual experience correlating attention-related body sensations that emerge with external visual stimuli resulting the improvement of attention. The attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is one of the most common mental health disorders among children. It includes symptoms such as difficulty paying attention, hyperactivity and impulsive behavior. The disease appears before age of seven and lasts till adulthood. In contrast with traditional treatment (medication) our work focuses on the usage of biometric marker such as heart rate variability, applied in recovery through other treatments such as art therapy based on cinematic language techniques. We will be able to create a database that can be used to forecast pathologies within the autism spectrum and ADHD using various machine learning algorithm, by expanding the pilot project and including more participants.

articleTitle: Research on the Analysis and Evaluation of the Performance of the Prosthetic Foot
abstract: A healthy foot has steps, a full support period, a one-leg support period, a longer pre-swing load, and a lower load response. In the case of prosthetic wearers, changes may occur in these parameters showing inadequate control and confidence in the prosthetic limb as well as the poor function of the ankle during the pre-swing and heel strike phases. Walking symmetry was analyzed by comparing left-right (amputated - healthy). Specific gait parameters were measured and evaluated using Tekscan's F-scan equipment for five prosthetic feet from different manufacturers. The main objective of the submitted article is to provide a comparative study in which the performance of foot prostheses is evaluated with computerized techniques for measuring plantar pressure.

articleTitle: Review of the Evaluation Methods for Stress, Anxiety, and Depression Levels
abstract: Nowadays, everyone experiences stress and anxiety occasionally. The main difference is that stress is generally a response to a threat, and anxiety is a stress reaction. Stress, anxiety, and depression are recognized as global disorders. Therefore, it is essential to reduce it as much as possible. Clinical psychological tests have been introduced to quantify stress, anxiety, and depression levels. These lend support to specialists in treating patients suffering from one or all these disorders. Thus, this review aims to present some tests used nationally, in Romania, and internationally, to assess the patient's degree of impairment and to determine if one of the tests can differentiate these diseases better based on their symptoms.

articleTitle: Radiological Diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 Infected Patients by Automated Classification of Chest Radiographs using DTL
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 is a strain of coronavirus in the Orthocoronavirinae subfamily, which was first identified in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. COVID-19 is the name of the disease produced by SARS-CoV-2. Because SARS-CoV-2 is cytopathic to airway epithelial cells and alveolar cells, researchers showed that combining features extracted from radiographic images with laboratory results may significantly aid in the early detection of the infection. Standard features seen in radiographs of patients with coronavirus are infiltrated or patchy opacities, like several features of other forms of viral pneumonia. In the early stages of COVID-19 infection, no abnormalities can be observed on radiographic images. However, as the disease unfolds, COVID-19 progressively manifests as a typical unilateral inflammation involving the middle and upper or lower lungs, sometimes with consolidation. Almost every hospital has at least one radiographer routinely used for diagnosing pneumonia, lymph nodes, and other conditions. Unfortunately, acquiring radiographic images and analyzing COVID-19 analyzing by a radiologist is time-consuming. Therefore, this work aims to assess the detection capability of the viral respiratory disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus from radiographic images using a deep transfer learning model implemented in a development environment for numerical computation and statistical analysis called MATLAB.

articleTitle: Interpretable Estimation of the Risk of Heart Failure Hospitalization from a 30-Second Electrocardiogram
abstract: Survival modeling in healthcare relies on explainable statistical models; yet, their underlying assumptions are often simplistic and, thus, unrealistic. Machine learning models can estimate more complex relationships and lead to more accurate predictions, but are non-interpretable. This study shows it is possible to estimate hospitalization for congestive heart failure by a 30 seconds single-lead electrocardiogram signal. Using a machine learning approach not only results in greater predictive power but also provides clinically meaningful interpretations. We train an eXtreme Gradient Boosting accelerated failure time model and exploit SHapley Additive exPlanations values to explain the effect of each feature on predictions. Our model achieved a concordance index of 0.828 and an area under the curve of 0.853 at one year and 0.858 at two years on a held-out test set of 6,573 patients. These results show that a rapid test based on an electrocardiogram could be crucial in targeting and treating high-risk individuals.

articleTitle: Molecular and Clinical Aspects in The Concept of Healthy Ageing
abstract: Both enthusiasm and concerns are raised considering that people worldwide are living longer. As the pace of population ageing is much faster than in the past, major challenges are posed for most of the countries: health is essential, yet there is little evidence that the quality of life is significantly better for the contemporary elderly. A healthy ageing is defined as the process of developing and maintaining the functional ability that enables wellbeing in older age. Many studies are focusing to the research of the telomeres and telomerase, which proved to bring hope for a healthy ageing. At cellular lever, there are many changes associated with the process of senescence, including genomic instability, telomere attrition, epigenetic alterations, mitochondrial dysfunction, altered intercellular communication, stem cell exhaustion. Among these hallmarks of aging, probably the one that received the biggest attention in the recent years is telomere attrition. Multiple studies has shown correlations between the presence of short telomeres and premature onset of diseases normally occurring at advanced age, such as type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular diseases, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, aplastic anemia. The effects that certain lifestyles may have upon health and longevity of individuals may be associated to accelerated telomeres shortening, that may lead to an early onset of age-associated diseases. Although there is substantial evidence that links the biology of telomeres with the process of aging, the molecular mechanisms are complex, which led to some contradictory study findings. Of the few strategies available that target the implication of telomeres biology in aging and disease, a number of products that are associated with an enhancing of telomerase function are used. Among these, cycloastragenol, has been shown to activate telomerase and elongate telomeres.

articleTitle: Web Based Medical System for Remote Heart Rate Monitoring with Cloud Integration
abstract: In this paper it is described the design and realization of a remote heart rate monitoring system, based on wireless devices, capable to measure and wirelessly transmit patient's heart rate (HR) to a cloud based database. The proposed system is used for long-term continuous monitoring of the patient as a diagnostic procedure and consists of several commercially available hardware for HR acquisition and custom developed software for data transmission through widely used Android-based smartphones to cloud based database. The patient's heart rate is stored in cloud and analyzed by a custom developed web application running on the medical doctors' computers. The patient monitoring device consists of a commercially purchased smartwatch, a smartphone, a gateway located in the cloud, and a graphical interface. A medical alert is sent in the interface when the HR is outside of the normally range values.

articleTitle: Psychological Implications of the Covid-19 Pandemic on Dental Students and Dentists
abstract: This study assessed the psychological impact of 91 students and 89 dentists during the Covid-19 pandemic through an anonymous online questionnaire. Statistical processing was done in SPSS 26.0. The psychological impact on dental students and dentists due to the Covid-19 pandemic was moderate; negative sensations of insecurity, stress, nervousness and feelings of sadness were moderate (scores≥3). The fear of infection with the SarS-CoV-2 virus from patients was moderate (scores≥3), but the fear of infecting close people was high (scores≥4), Concerns about their families' health problems were also increased (scores≥4). Students and dentists did not regret choosing this profession and did not lose control over their lives (scores≥1), Respondents' answers correlated statistically significantly with some independent socio-demographic variables (p≤0.05). Our study revealed that the Covid-19 pandemic had a negative impact on the psychological health of dental students and dentists, who had moderate symptoms and signs of stress and anxiety than of depression, but they knew how to control their lives despite the dangers of the Covid-19 pandemic.

articleTitle: Nailfold Video Capillaroscopy for the Analysis of Microcirculation
abstract: Nailfold video capillaroscopy (NVC) is a noninvasive diagnostic tool for the analysis of microcirculation. Microcirculation analysis and follow-up is of fundamental importance for individuation and/or monitoring the onset of a pathological condition and its progression. Raynaud's phenomenon as a possible association with scleroderma, lupus erythematosus, diabetes mellitus, etc. can be assessed by NVC. Although NVC-based analysis is clinically validated for the detection of some diseases (e.g., systemic sclerosis, scleroderma, etc.), even in the early stages, its use is currently limited and poorly widespread. Hereafter, the development of a nailfold capillaroscope, working at 540 nm is presented. A proper signal processing based on multivariate analysis to allow its use also in a non specialistic hospital setting. The realized system is intended to help the user in its interpretation and, at the same time, allows the monitor the values.
